text:
- The following is a conversation
with Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, one of the most
important and influential companies in the history
of human civilization. NVIDIA is the engine powering
the AI revolution, and a lot of its success can be directly
attributed to Jensen's sheer force of will and his many brilliant bets and decisions
as a leader, engineer, and innovator. This is Lex Fridman Podcast. And now
dear friends, here's Jensen Huang. You've propelled NVIDIA into a new era in AI, moving beyond its focus on chip
scale design to now rack scale design. And I think it's fair to
say that winning for NVIDIA for a long time used to be about building
the best GPU possible, and you still do, but now you've expanded
that to extreme co-design of GPU, CPU memory, networking,
storage, power cooling, software, the rack itself, the pod
that you've announced, and even the data center. So let's talk about
extreme co-design. What is the hardest part of co-designing
system with that many complex components and design variables?
speaker: Lex Fridman
text_tr: - Aşağıdaki konuşma, insanlık tarihinin en önemli ve etkili şirketlerinden biri olan NVIDIA'nın CEO'su Jensen Huang ile bir sohbet. NVIDIA, AI devrimini destekleyen motor ve başarısının büyük bir kısmı, Jensen'ın iradesi ve lider, mühendis ve yenilikçi olarak yaptığı birçok parlak tahmin ve karara doğrudan atfedilebilir. Bu Lex Fridman Podcast. Ve şimdi sevgili arkadaşlar, işte Jensen Huang. NVIDIA'yı AI'da yeni bir çağa taşıdınız, çip ölçeği tasarımına odaklanmaktan, şimdi raf ölçeği tasarımına geçtiniz. Ve uzun bir süre için NVIDIA'nın kazanmasının en iyi GPU'yu inşa etmekle ilgili olduğunu söylemek adil, hala öyle, ama şimdi bunu GPU, CPU bellek, ağ, depolama, güç soğutma, yazılım, rafın kendisi, duyurduğunuz pod ve hatta veri merkezi ile aşırı birlikte tasarıma genişlettiniz. O halde aşırı birlikte tasarımı konuşalım. Bu kadar karmaşık bileşen ve tasarım değişkeni ile sistem tasarlamanın en zor kısmı nedir?

- And then that became the platform and the
foundation for the deep learning revolution. - That was also another great,
great observation. Yeah. - That existential moment, do you
remember... Like, what were those meetings like? What were those discussions like,
deciding as a company, risking everything? - Well I had to make it clear to the
board what we're trying to do, and the management team knew our gross
margins were gonna get crushed. So you could imagine a world
where GeForce would carry the burden of CUDA and
none of the gamers would appreciate it and none of the gamers
would pay for it. You know, they only pay certain price and it doesn't matter what
your cost is. And so the... You know, we, we increased our cost
by 50% and that con- consumed... And we were a 35%
gross margin company, and so it, it was a... It was quite a
difficult decision to make. But you could imagine that someday this would
go into workstations and it would go into supercomputers and, and in those segments,
maybe we can capture more margin.
speaker: Jensen Huang

- Yeah, yeah. Yeah, we have
more scaling laws now. - So I think you've outlined four of them
with pre-training, post-training, test time, and agentic scaling. What do you
think, when you think about the future, deep future and the near-term
future, what are the blockers that you're most concerned about that keep
you up at night that you have to overcome in order to keep scaling? - Well, we can go back and reflect on
what people thought were blockers. So in the beginning, we were the
first... The pre-training scaling law. You know, people
thought well rightfully so, that the amount of data that
we have, high-quality data that we have will limit the intelligence that
we achieve. And that scaling law was an important, very important
scaling law. The larger the model, the correspondingly more data
results in a better... With a results in a smarter AI. And
so that was pre-training. And Ilya Sutskever, Ilya said, "We're out of data,"
or something like that. "Pre-training is over," or something like
that. The industry panicked, you know, that this is the end of AI.
And of course, of course that, that's obviously not true. We're gonna keep
on scaling the amount of data that we have to, to train with. A lot of that
data is probably gonna be synthetic, and that also confused people,
you know? And what people don't realize is they've kind of
forgotten that most of the data that, that we are training that
we teach each other with, inform each other with, is
synthetic. You know, I...
speaker: Jensen Huang
claim: There are misconceptions about data limitations in AI development, and scaling will continue despite concerns.
claim_silver: There are misconceptions about data limitations in AI development, and scaling will continue despite concerns.
text_tr: - Evet, evet. Evet, şimdi daha fazla ölçekleme yasamız var. - Yani, ön eğitim, son eğitim, test zamanı ve ajans ölçekleme ile dört tanesini belirttiğinizi düşünüyorum. Geleceği düşündüğünüzde, derin gelecekte ve yakın gelecekte, sizi en çok endişelendiren ve gece uykunuzu kaçıran engeller nelerdir, bunları aşmanız gerekiyor ki ölçeklemeye devam edebilesiniz? - Şey, geri dönüp insanların engel olarak düşündüklerine yansıyabiliriz. Başlangıçta, biz ilk... Ön eğitim ölçekleme yasası. Biliyorsunuz, insanlar haklı olarak, sahip olduğumuz veri miktarının, sahip olduğumuz yüksek kaliteli verinin, ulaşacağımız zekayı sınırlayacağını düşündüler. Ve o ölçekleme yasası çok önemliydi. Model ne kadar büyükse, o kadar fazla veri daha iyi sonuçlar verir... Daha akıllı bir AI ile sonuçlanır. Ve bu ön eğitimdi. Ilya Sutskever, Ilya, "Verimiz bitti," ya da buna benzer bir şey söyledi. "Ön eğitim sona erdi," ya da buna benzer bir şey. Endüstri panikledi, biliyorsunuz, bu AI'nın sonu. Ve elbette, bu kesinlikle doğru değil. Sahip olduğumuz veri miktarını artırmaya devam edeceğiz. Bu verilerin çoğu muhtemelen sentetik olacak ve bu da insanları karıştırdı, biliyorsunuz? Ve insanların fark etmediği şey, birbirimize öğrettiğimiz, birbirimizi bilgilendirdiğimiz verilerin çoğunun sentetik olduğudur. Biliyorsunuz, ben...

It's synthetic because it
didn't come out of nature. You created it. I'm consuming
it. I modify it, augment it, I regenerate it, somebody
else consumes it. And so, so we've now reached a level where AI is able
to take ground truth, augment it...... Enhance it, synthetically
generate an enormous amount of data. And that part of post-training continues to scale, and so the
amount of data that we could use that is human generated will be
smaller, and smaller, and smaller. The amount of data that
we use to train model, is going to continue to scale to the
point where we're no longer limited... Training is no longer limited by...
Data is now limited by compute. And the reason for that is most of the data
is synthetic. Then the next phase is test time, and I still remember people telling me
that, "Inference? Oh, yeah, that's easy. Pre-training, that's hard." These
are giant systems that people are talking about. Inference must be easy. And so
inference chips are gonna be little tiny chips, and ... you know, they're not, they're not like
NVIDIA's chips. Oh, those are gonna be complicated and expensive, and, you
know, we could make... And this is- in the future, inference is gonna be the
biggest market, and it's gonna be easy, and we're gonna commoditize it. You know,
everybody can build their own chips. And, and that was always illogical to
me because inference is thinking, and I think thinking is hard.
Thinking is way harder than reading.
speaker: Jensen Huang
claim: Inference in AI is more complex than people think, and the future of AI will rely heavily on synthetic data and compute rather than human-generated data.
claim_silver: Inference in AI is more complex than people think, and the future of AI will rely heavily on synthetic data and compute rather than human-generated data.
text_tr: Bu sentetik çünkü doğadan çıkmadı. Siz onu yarattınız. Ben onu tüketiyorum. Ben onu değiştiriyorum, artırıyorum, yeniden üretiyorum, bir başkası onu tüketiyor. Ve şimdi AI'nın gerçek veriyi alıp artırabildiği, onu geliştirebildiği, sentetik olarak muazzam miktarda veri üretebildiği bir seviyeye ulaştık. Ve bu son eğitim kısmı ölçeklenmeye devam ediyor, bu yüzden model eğitmek için kullandığımız insan tarafından üretilen veri miktarı daha küçük, daha küçük, daha küçük olacak. Modeli eğitmek için kullandığımız veri miktarı, artık sınırlı olmayacak... Eğitim artık veri ile sınırlı değil. Veri artık hesaplama ile sınırlı. Bunun nedeni, verilerin çoğunun sentetik olması. Sonraki aşama test zamanı ve hala insanların bana "Çıkarım? Oh, evet, bu kolay. Ön eğitim, bu zor." dediğini hatırlıyorum. Bunlar insanların konuştuğu devasa sistemler. Çıkarım kolay olmalı. Ve bu yüzden çıkarım çipleri küçük çipler olacak, ve... biliyorsunuz, NVIDIA'nın çipleri gibi değiller. Oh, bunlar karmaşık ve pahalı olacak, ve biliyorsunuz, yapabiliriz... Ve bu gelecekte, çıkarım en büyük pazar olacak ve kolay olacak, ve bunu standart hale getireceğiz. Biliyorsunuz, herkes kendi çiplerini yapabilir. Ve bu her zaman mantıksız geliyordu çünkü çıkarım düşünmektir ve bence düşünmek zordur. Düşünmek okumaktan çok daha zordur.

text:
You know, pre-training is just memorization and generalization, you know,
and looking for patterns in relationships. You're reading and reading, versus thinking,
reasoning, solving problems, taking unexplored experiences,
new experiences, and breaking it down into...
Decomposing it into, you know, solvable pieces that we
then go off, either through first principle reasoning, or, you
know, through previous examples, prior experiences. You know, or just uh, exploration and search and,
you know, trying different things. And that whole process
of, of test time scaling, Inference, is really about
thinking. And it's about reasoning, it's about planning, it's about
search, it's about... And so how could that possibly be compute light? And
we were absolutely right about that. You know, so test time scaling
is intensely compute intensive. Then the question is, okay, now we're at inference
and we're at test time scaling, what's beyond that?
speaker: Lex Fridman
claim: Test time scaling and inference in AI require significant computational resources and cannot be compute light.
claim_silver: Test time scaling and inference in AI require significant computational resources and cannot be compute light.
text_tr: Biliyorsunuz, ön eğitim sadece ezberleme ve genelleme, biliyorsunuz, ilişkilerdeki kalıpları aramakla ilgilidir. Okuyorsunuz ve okuyorsunuz, düşünmek, akıl yürütmek, problem çözmek, keşfedilmemiş deneyimleri, yeni deneyimleri alıp bunları... Çözülmesi mümkün parçalara ayırmakla ilgilidir. Biliyorsunuz, ya birinci ilke akıl yürütmesi ile ya da önceki örnekler, önceki deneyimler ile. Biliyorsunuz, ya da sadece keşif ve arama ve... biliyorsunuz, farklı şeyler denemek. Ve bu test zamanı ölçekleme süreci, çıkarım, gerçekten düşünmekle ilgilidir. Ve bu akıl yürütme ile ilgilidir, planlama ile ilgilidir, arama ile ilgilidir, ve bu yüzden bunun nasıl hesaplama açısından hafif olabileceğini düşünemiyorum. Ve bu konuda kesinlikle haklıydık. Biliyorsunuz, test zamanı ölçekleme yoğun bir hesaplama gerektiriyor. O zaman soru şu, tamam, şimdi çıkarımdayız ve test zamanı ölçeklemesindeyiz, bunun ötesinde ne var?

And out of those two out of three
capabilities, we also give you access control based on whatever rights that
you're given by enterprise. And then we connect it to a policy engine
that all these enterprises already have. And so we're going to try to do our best
to help OpenClaw become a better claw. - So you eloquently explained
how we have a long history of blockers that we thought were going to be blockers,
and we overcame them. But now looking into the future, what do you think might be the
blockers now that it's clear that agents will be everywhere? So obviously we're going to need
compute. So what is going to be the blocker for that scaling? - Power is a concern, but it's not the
only concern. But that's the reason why we're pushing so hard on extreme co-design,
so that we can improve the tokens per second per watt orders of magnitude every single year. And so in
the last 10 years, Moore's Law would have progressed computing
about 100 times in the last 10 years. We progressed
and scaled up computing by a million times in the last 10 years.
And so we're gonna keep on doing that through extreme co-design. So
energy efficiency, perf per watt, completely affects the
revenues of a company. It affects the revenues of a
factory. And we're just going to push that to the limit so that we
can keep on driving token costs down as fast as we can. You know, the our computer price is going
up, but our token generation effectiveness is going up so
much faster that token cost is coming down. It's just coming down
an order of magnitude every year.
speaker: Jensen Huang
claim: Energy efficiency and compute scaling are critical for the future of AI agents.
claim_silver: Energy efficiency and compute scaling are critical for the future of AI agents.

- I think that NVIDIA's growth is Extremely
likely, and in my mind, inevitable. And let me explain why. We're the
largest computer company in history. That alone should beg the question, why? And the reason of course... Two reasons.
First, two foundational technical reasons. The first reason is that computing went
from being a retrieval-based, file retrieval system. Almost everything is
a file... We pre-write something, we pre-record something. You know, we draw
something, we put it on the web, we put it in a file. And we use a
recommender system, some smart filter, to figure out what to
retrieve for you. And so we were a pre-recording, human
pre-recording, and file retrieving system. That's what a
computer is, largely. To now, AI computers
are contextually aware, which means that it has to process
and generate tokens in real time. So we went from a retrieval-based
computing system to a generative-based computing system.
speaker: Jensen Huang
claim: NVIDIA's growth is inevitable due to advancements in AI computing.
claim_silver: NVIDIA's growth is inevitable due to advancements in AI computing.
